results.summary_before: This design generates a 640x480 VGA signal at 25.175 MHz showing the letters IEEE bouncing around the screen. It has no user controls and simply runs from the clock and reset, with the eight outputs wired to the Tiny VGA PMOD pinout. The only external hardware needed is a VGA PMOD and a compatible monitor. The documentation is very thin, noting only that the Verilog was produced with Gemini, so little can be said about the internal implementation.

results.summary_before: This is a two-channel byte DMA engine that moves data to and from an external SPI PSRAM device. Configuration bytes are loaded on the input pins with a valid strobe, a start pin triggers operation, and the SPI master pins connect to the memory. Status outputs report DMA activity, completion pulses per channel, pending configuration and configuration errors. It targets a QSPI PMOD with an APS6404 PSRAM used in single-bit SPI mode, and the documentation covers the pin mapping but not the internal architecture or measured throughput.

results.summary_before: This design implements a Hamming(7,4) error-correcting code system that can encode 4-bit data into a 7-bit codeword and decode a received codeword while detecting and correcting a single-bit error. A MODE input selects between encoding and decoding, and an error flag output indicates when a correctable error was detected. No external hardware is required beyond input switches and LEDs to observe the encoded or corrected output. The documentation is very short and does not describe the internal implementation or provide test vectors.
